inputs.text: Thousands of people who showed up in immigration court seeking legal status were arrested and detained instead. Court documents reportedly indicate prosecutors acknowledged the May memo did not authorize those arrests, yet ICE lawyers allegedly used it to defend them. That is not a mere paperwork dispute: it reflects an enforcement system that can turn access to due process into a risk for people already made vulnerable. People should not be punished for seeking legal protection. We need accountability and safeguards that prevent immigration enforcement from using the courts as a trap.
